notes: Interface facts only: primitive names, grammar shapes, option and keyword names, and the observed behaviour of Stata 19.5. No StataCorp prose, tables or examples are copied.
sources entries are 'sthlp:<path under source_root>' for a help file and 'targets:<subject>' for a subject key in qa/stata_targets.json.

openstat_status is derived by reading openstat/*.py and, where cheap, by running a probe through Engine. 'partial' means the primitive exists but a documented case diverges; the divergence is named in openstat_note.

areas.title: if / in qualifiers
areas.summary: Observation selection shared by every command that takes a varlist.

areas.title: by / bysort
areas.summary: Repeat a command over groups of observations.

areas.title: Weights (aw / fw / pw / iw)
areas.summary: The bracketed weight specification and the four weight types.

areas.title: Factor variables
areas.summary: Indicator, continuous, base-level and interaction terms.

areas.title: Time-series operators
areas.summary: L. F. D. S. and the operator-numlist / repeated-operator forms.

areas.title: Storage types
areas.summary: byte / int / long / float / double / str# / strL and how they are set.

areas.title: Display formats
areas.summary: The %fmt grammar and the rendering rules behind it.

areas.title: r() / e() / s() / c()
areas.summary: Stored-result classes and macro versus expression position.

areas.title: Command prefixes
areas.summary: capture, quietly, noisily, version, statsby, svy, mi, bayes.

areas.summary: The syntax command and its element / option descriptors.

areas.title: Mata subset
areas.summary: The Stata interface functions and the matrix constructors.

areas.title: Command groups
areas.summary: Data, estimation, postestimation, graphics and programming commands.

primitives.name: if_qualifier
primitives.summary: Runs the command on the observations for which exp is true; exp is evaluated on the whole dataset first, then intersected with any in range.
examples: regress y z if g == 1 & y > 2
primitives.openstat_note: openstat/engine.py Engine.qualifiers() splits the argument list on a top-level ' if ' outside quotes and parentheses; the mask is combined with &=. Engine._keep_drop() and Engine._describe() are the main call sites.

primitives.name: in_qualifier
primitives.summary: Restricts a command to an observation-number range. f means the first observation, l the last, negative numbers count back from the end.
primitives.openstat_note: openstat/engine.py Engine.qualifiers() accepts (-?\d+|f|l)(/(-?\d+|f|l))?. GAP: observation 0 is accepted and yields an empty selection; Stata 19.5 rejects 'in 0/2' with rc 198 "'0' invalid observation number".

primitives.name: if_in_combination
primitives.summary: A command may carry both qualifiers; the effective sample is the intersection of the two selections, and if is evaluated over all observations.
primitives.openstat_note: openstat/engine.py Engine.qualifiers(): every qualifier found at top level is ANDed into one boolean mask before the command body runs.

primitives.name: by_prefix
primitives.summary: Runs the command once per group of the varlist. Data must already be sorted by the varlist (rc 5 otherwise) unless bysort or the sort option is used.
primitives.openstat_note: openstat/engine.py Engine._by() accepts only {egen, generate, replace, summarize, count, assert, tabulate, list, total, mean} as the body. GAP: 'by g: regress y z' is rc 199 here, rc 0 in Stata, and no block form ('by g: { ... }') is recognised.

primitives.name: bysort_prefix
primitives.summary: Sorts the data by the varlist and then runs the command once per group; the sort is stable and happens before the first group runs.
primitives.openstat_note: openstat/engine.py Engine._by(sort=True): sorts with sort_values(..., kind='stable', na_position='last') and concatenates the per-group results. Same body-command allow-list as by_prefix.

primitives.name: by_sort_override
primitives.summary: The parenthesised second varlist selects the order the groups are processed in without changing the grouping.
primitives.openstat_note: openstat/engine.py Engine._by() sorts by varlist1 + varlist2 together rather than by varlist2 inside each group; the observed output matches a full sort for the probed cases but the two orderings differ when varlist1 and varlist2 conflict. Would be settled by a conformance case with two group variables and a sort variable.

primitives.name: by_unsorted_error
primitives.summary: A plain by on data that is not sorted by the varlist fails with rc 5 instead of sorting silently.
primitives.openstat_note: openstat/engine.py Engine._by(): compares the sort keys before and after sorting and raises StataError('not sorted', 5).

primitives.name: weight_bracket
primitives.summary: A bracketed weight specification that follows the varlist and precedes the comma: [aw=w], [fw=w], [pw=w], [iw=w].
primitives.openstat_note: openstat/design.py parse_weight() strips the bracket from the model specification and returns (text, kind, expression); used by statistics.py, panel.py and instrumental.py. GAP: it is not a general command-level parser, so in descriptive commands 'summarize y [fw=w]' the bracket is read as a varlist and w is summarized as a second variable.

primitives.name: weight_aweight
primitives.summary: Analytic weights scale the contribution of each observation; the variance formula treats them as inverse-variance information.
primitives.openstat_note: openstat/design.py parse_weight() -> 'aw'; statistics.py applies the weight in the estimator. Applied (weighted SEs differ from the unweighted fit) but the weighted point estimates have not been compared with Stata numerically.

primitives.name: weight_fweight
primitives.summary: Frequency weights state how many observations each row stands for; N becomes the sum of the weights.
primitives.openstat_note: openstat/design.py parse_weight() -> 'fw'. In estimation the weight is applied; in 'summarize' r(N) stays the row count (Stata reports the weight sum: measured 12 vs 6 on the same data).

primitives.name: weight_pweight
primitives.summary: Sampling weights describe the inverse probability of selection; the variance is computed from the weighted estimator, not from the weight sums.
primitives.openstat_note: openstat/design.py parse_weight() -> 'pw'; statistics.py applies it. The weighted SE differs from aweight, as in Stata, but no numeric comparison against Stata has been recorded.

primitives.name: weight_iweight
primitives.summary: Importance weights are accepted only by a few commands and are refused elsewhere with an explicit error.
primitives.openstat_note: openstat/design.py parse_weight() recognises 'iw' but the estimator raises StataError('importance weights not yet implemented', 199); measured on 'regress y z [iw=w]'.

primitives.name: fv_i
primitives.summary: Expands a categorical variable into one indicator per level, omitting the base level; the omitted level is reported with a b coefficient of 0.
primitives.openstat_note: openstat/design.py build_design()/atom() when prefix == 'i'. Works in the estimation commands that call build_design (regress, logit, ivregress, xtreg, ...), not in descriptive or data commands: 'summarize i.g' is rc 111 here and rc 0 in Stata.

primitives.name: fv_c
primitives.summary: Treats a variable as continuous inside a factor specification, which matters only when it is combined with ## or #.
primitives.openstat_note: openstat/design.py atom(): prefix 'c' returns the raw values; inside an interaction the column is named 'c.name'.

primitives.name: fv_ib_base
primitives.summary: Chooses the base (omitted) level: a specific value, the smallest value (default), or the largest value.
primitives.openstat_note: openstat/design.py atom(): prefix ib<digits>, 'b<digits>', 'ib(first)' and 'ib(last)' select the base and record omitted['<base>b.<name>'] = 0.

primitives.name: fv_ibn
primitives.summary: Includes an indicator for every level, leaving no base level and dropping the constant implicitly.
primitives.openstat_note: openstat/design.py atom(): prefix 'ibn' sets selected = all levels and base = None.

primitives.name: fv_ib_freq
primitives.summary: Uses the most frequent level as the base.
primitives.openstat_note: openstat/design.py atom() has no 'ib(freq)' branch; 'regress y ib(freq).g' falls through to the varlist lookup and fails with rc 111 'variable ib(freq).g not found'. Stata runs it with rc 0.

primitives.name: fv_o
primitives.summary: Selects the levels to omit; the o. operator implies i. for the levels that are kept.
primitives.openstat_note: openstat/design.py atom() has no 'o' branch; 'regress y o2.g' is rc 111 here, rc 0 in Stata.

primitives.name: fv_hash
primitives.summary: Builds the interaction of the listed terms only; each factor contributes its indicators and the product is one column per cell.
primitives.openstat_note: openstat/design.py build_design() add(): splits on '#' and multiplies the per-term columns; interaction columns are named 'a#b'. Up to eight-way interactions are accepted.

primitives.name: fv_doublehash
primitives.summary: Expands to every main effect and interaction implied by the terms: a##b means a, b and a#b.
primitives.openstat_note: openstat/design.py build_design(): '##' is expanded over combinations() of the factors, then each subset is added as a # interaction.

primitives.name: fv_numlist
primitives.summary: Selects a list or range of levels to include, or the nth ordered value as the base.
primitives.openstat_note: openstat/design.py atom() regex (i|c|ibn|ib(\d+|\(first\)|\(last\))|b\d+|\d+)\. does not match 'i(1/2).' or 'ib(#2).'; both are rc 111 here and rc 0 in Stata.

primitives.name: fv_omitted_coefficient
primitives.summary: The base level appears in the coefficient vector as a zero so that _b[1b.g] resolves.
primitives.openstat_note: openstat/design.py atom(): values are put in the Design.omitted dict; the coefficient vector built by statistics.py carries the base entries.

primitives.name: ts_L
primitives.summary: Lag: the value of the variable # periods earlier. L. equals L1. and L0. is the variable itself; a missing period yields a missing value.
primitives.openstat_note: openstat/design.py time_series(): kind 'L' shifts the time key by +count and merges back on (panel, time), so gaps stay missing.

primitives.name: ts_F
primitives.summary: Lead: the value # periods later, the complement of L.
primitives.openstat_note: openstat/design.py time_series(): kind 'F' shifts the time key by -count.

primitives.name: ts_D
primitives.summary: Difference: var_t - var_(t-#); D1. equals S1.
primitives.openstat_note: openstat/design.py time_series(): kind 'D' applies the one-period difference count times.

primitives.name: ts_S
primitives.summary: Seasonal difference: var_t - var_(t-#). S1 equals D1, S2 is not D2.
primitives.openstat_note: openstat/design.py time_series(): kind 'S' re-applies the one-period difference count times, so it computes D# instead of the offset difference. Measured: S2.y on y = 2*_n is 4 in Stata (y5 - y3) and 0 here.

primitives.name: ts_numlist
primitives.summary: An operator followed by a numlist means the set of operated variables: L(1/3).x is L.x L2.x L3.x.
primitives.openstat_note: openstat/design.py time_series() matches only operator#.var, so in a varlist 'list y L(2).y' is rc 111 'variable L(2).y not found' while Stata lists the lagged column; in an expression Stata itself rejects it with r(133) unknown function L().

primitives.name: ts_repeat
primitives.summary: Operators may be repeated and combined; Stata canonicalises the sequence into the equivalent single operator.
primitives.openstat_note: openstat/design.py time_series() takes one operator letter only; 'list y LLL.y' is rc 111 'variable LLL.y not found'.

primitives.name: ts_requires_tsset
primitives.summary: Any time-series operator needs a declared time variable; without one the command stops instead of guessing an ordering.
primitives.openstat_note: openstat/design.py time_series(): raises StataError('time variable not set; use tsset or xtset', 111) when no time key is registered; tsset and xtset both register one (openstat/panel.py).

primitives.name: type_byte
primitives.summary: One-byte integer storage, range -127..100, default format %8.0g; an out-of-range value becomes missing rather than being clamped.
primitives.openstat_note: openstat/generation.py _generate() uses storage.INTEGER_RANGE and storage.DEFAULT_FORMAT; measured 'generate byte b9 = 1e10' -> . and describe reports byte %8.0g.

primitives.name: type_int
primitives.summary: Two-byte integer storage, range -32767..32740, default format %8.0g.
primitives.openstat_note: openstat/generation.py _generate() + openstat/storage.py INTEGER_RANGE; describe reports int %8.0g.

primitives.name: type_long
primitives.summary: Four-byte integer storage, range -2147483647..2147483620, default format %12.0g.
primitives.openstat_note: openstat/generation.py _generate() + openstat/storage.py; describe reports long %12.0g.

primitives.name: type_float
primitives.summary: Single-precision storage, default format %9.0g; this is what an untyped generate creates.
primitives.openstat_note: openstat/generation.py _generate(): storage defaults to openstat/storage.py DEFAULT_TYPE ('float') unless 'set type' changed it.

primitives.name: type_double
primitives.summary: Double-precision storage, default format %10.0g.
primitives.openstat_note: openstat/generation.py _generate(); describe reports double %10.0g.

primitives.name: type_str
primitives.summary: Fixed-width string storage; values longer than the declared width are truncated to it.
primitives.openstat_note: openstat/generation.py _generate() matches 'str\d*' and describe reports str3 %9s.

primitives.name: type_strL
primitives.summary: Long string storage for values longer than 2045 bytes; it has no fixed declared width.
primitives.openstat_note: openstat/generation.py accepts the 'strL' token and describe reports strL, but the column is an ordinary Python object column: there is no 2045-byte boundary check and no distinct strL read/write path.

primitives.name: type_recast
primitives.summary: Changes a variable's storage type in place, refusing conversions that would lose information unless force is given.
primitives.openstat_note: openstat/extended_data.py _recast(): rewrites the column and storage_types; rc 459 'recast would lose information; specify force' when values change. compress is implemented as well (extended_data._compress()) and picks the smallest type that holds the values.

primitives.name: fmt_g
primitives.summary: General format: the fewest characters that identify the value, switching to scientific notation by Stata's rules; the digit model is documented in docs/formats.md and reproduced exactly.
primitives.openstat_note: openstat/formats.py _general()/format_value(); the %g model is checked byte-for-byte against Stata 19.5. Measured live: %9.3g 3.14159265 -> '     3.14' and %9.0g 123456789.5 -> ' 1.23e+08' in both runtimes.

primitives.name: fmt_f
primitives.summary: Fixed point with d digits after the decimal point, right justified in w columns; a leading 0 in the width keeps the field zero-filled.
primitives.openstat_note: openstat/formats.py format_value() kind 'f' formats with Python and pads with spaces only. GAP: '%06.2f 3.5' renders '3.50' here and '003.50' in Stata, so the zero-fill flag is ignored.

primitives.name: fmt_e
primitives.summary: Scientific notation with d digits after the decimal point and a two-digit, sign-prefixed exponent.
primitives.openstat_note: openstat/formats.py format_value() else-branch uses precision-1 digits, strips trailing zeros and prints the exponent without zero padding. GAP: '%12.4e 31415.9265' renders '3.142e+4' here and '  3.1416e+04' in Stata.

primitives.name: fmt_s
primitives.summary: String format: right justified in w columns, truncating or padding as declared.
primitives.openstat_note: openstat/formats.py is_text_format()/format_value() (the string branch requires a %s format and raises FormatError otherwise).

primitives.name: fmt_c
primitives.summary: The c suffix inserts thousands separators in the integer part.
primitives.openstat_note: openstat/formats.py _group(); measured '%8.0gc 1000' -> '1,000' and '%12.2fc 12345.678' -> '12,345.68'.

primitives.name: fmt_date
primitives.summary: Date and time formats render a numeric value as a calendar date or timestamp with a chosen sub-format.
primitives.openstat_note: openstat/formats.py knows the DATE regex (is_date_format) but format_value() has no date branch and raises FormatError('invalid %format %td'). 'format y %td' is accepted and then 'display y[1]' shows the plain number; 'display %td 20000' is rc 198 here and rc 0 in Stata.

primitives.name: fmt_widen
primitives.summary: A value that does not fit the declared width is widened, never truncated, and the field is right justified.
primitives.grammar: %w...   when the value needs more than w columns
primitives.openstat_note: openstat/formats.py format_value(): 'if len(text) > width: width = len(text)' then rjust(width).

primitives.name: rclass
primitives.summary: Results of general commands: r(N), r(mean), r(sum_w), r(Var), ... set by summarize, count, tabulate and the return command.
primitives.openstat_note: openstat/engine.py Engine.returns + expression.py Evaluator.result(group='r'); return list prints a Python dict, which is not Stata's layout.

primitives.name: eclass
primitives.summary: Results of estimation commands: e(N), e(r2), e(b), e(V), e(ll), e(df_r), ...
primitives.openstat_note: openstat/statistics.py stores into Engine.estimates; expression.py Evaluator.result(group='e'). 'return scalar' inside an eclass program still lands in r(), which Stata does not do.

primitives.name: sclass
primitives.summary: Results of parsing commands, listed with sreturn list.
primitives.openstat_note: openstat/macros.py _resolve_class handles r/e/c only, and expression.py Evaluator.result has no 's' group. Measured: 'display s(nosuch)' is rc 111 'nosuch not found' here (Stata: missing value, rc 0) and 'sreturn list' is rc 199.

primitives.name: cclass
primitives.summary: Session values: c(N), c(k), c(pi), c(version), c(flavor), c(pwd), c(rc), c(seed), c(filename), c(adopath), ...
primitives.openstat_note: openstat/cclass.py build_cclass() defines exactly the names Stata 19.5 defines; an unknown name in expression position raises rc 133, matching Stata. Documented divergences: c(seed) is the numeric seed rather than the hex RNG state, c(adopath) is OpenStat's ado directory, c(mode) is always 'batch'.

primitives.name: macro_position
primitives.summary: In macro position the value is text: the number rendered with %18.0g and the padding removed. An unset r()/e() name expands to nothing.
primitives.openstat_note: openstat/macros.py expand_macros()/_resolve_class(), MACRO_FORMAT = '%18.0g'; engine._macro_text() uses the same format. GAP: an unset *local* or *global* expands to the literal '`name'' here, where Stata expands it to the empty string.

primitives.name: expression_position
primitives.summary: In an expression the value is a number and is displayed with the default numeric format; an unset r()/e() is the missing value.
primitives.openstat_note: openstat/expression.py Evaluator.result(); parser_expr.py rewrites the reference into __result(group, key). Measured: 'display r(nosuch)' -> '.', 'display c(pi)' -> 3.1415927, both matching Stata 19.5.

primitives.name: result_listing
primitives.summary: Lists the stored results of the current class.
primitives.grammar: return list [, all] | ereturn list [, all] | sreturn list
primitives.openstat_note: openstat/engine.py _return()/_ereturn() emit a Python dict repr rather than Stata's aligned list; sreturn is rc 199.

primitives.name: prefix_capture
primitives.summary: Runs the command, suppresses its error, and leaves the return code in _rc so the caller can test it.
primitives.openstat_note: openstat/engine.py Engine.command(): catches StataError/MacroError/OSError and friends, sets self.rc from the exception (default 198). GAP: the block form 'capture { ... }' is not recognised (rc 199 'command { not implemented'); Stata accepts it with rc 0.

primitives.name: prefix_quietly
primitives.summary: Runs the command with its output suppressed; the results it stores remain available.
primitives.openstat_note: openstat/engine.py Engine.command() increments self._quiet before the call and restores it after; Engine.emit() drops output while _quiet > 0. GAP: 'quietly { ... }' blocks are not recognised (rc 199), Stata accepts them.

primitives.name: prefix_noisily
primitives.summary: Re-enables output for one command inside a quiet context.
primitives.openstat_note: openstat/engine.py Engine.command(): sets self._quiet = 0 for the duration of the command.

primitives.name: prefix_version
primitives.summary: Declares the Stata version the following code is written for; commands are then interpreted with that version's rules.
primitives.openstat_note: openstat/engine.py Engine.command(): accepts version <= 19.5, runs the rest of the line, and raises rc 9 'unsupported version request' above that. No per-version behaviour switch is applied.

primitives.name: prefix_statsby
primitives.summary: Runs a command per group and collects the stored results into a new dataset.
primitives.openstat_note: openstat/engine.py has no statsby branch; 'statsby, by(g): summarize y' is rc 199 here. Stata parses the prefix and runs it (rc 4 only because of an unrelated unsaved-data check).

primitives.name: prefix_svy
primitives.summary: Runs an estimation command with the survey design declared by svyset.
primitives.openstat_note: No svy branch in openstat/engine.py; 'svy: regress y z' is rc 199 here. Stata recognises the prefix and stops with rc 119 'data not set up for svy, use svyset'.

primitives.name: prefix_mi
primitives.summary: Runs a command on each multiply-imputed dataset and combines the results.
primitives.openstat_note: No mi branch in openstat/engine.py; 'mi estimate: regress y z' is rc 199 here. Stata recognises the prefix and stops with rc 119 'data not mi set'.

primitives.name: prefix_bayes
primitives.summary: Re-estimates a supported command as a Bayesian model by MCMC.
primitives.openstat_note: No bayes branch in openstat/engine.py; 'bayes: regress y z' is rc 199 here. Stata runs the full sampler (rc 0).

primitives.name: syntax_command
primitives.summary: Parses the program's argument list against a declared grammar and stores each matched piece in a local macro; a mismatch stops with rc 197 in Stata and rc 198 here.
primitives.openstat_note: openstat/syntax.py SyntaxCommand, invoked by Engine._syntax_command(); used by program bodies and by marksample via _syntax_marker().

primitives.name: syntax_varlist_element
primitives.summary: Declares which part of the argument list is a name list and binds it to a local of the same name; 'varname' requires exactly one name.
primitives.openstat_note: openstat/syntax.py _parse_elements()/SyntaxCommand.run(): names are resolved through Engine.varlist(); a missing required element raises 'varname required' (rc 100).

primitives.name: syntax_anything_element
primitives.summary: Captures the remaining argument text verbatim, optionally into a named local.
primitives.openstat_note: openstat/syntax.py run(): the 'anything' element stores the remaining text under the element (or its name= local).

primitives.name: syntax_ifin_elements
primitives.summary: Captures the if and in qualifiers as text, including the keyword, so the program can pass them on.
primitives.openstat_note: openstat/engine.py _syntax_command() stores _syntax_if/_syntax_in and the locals 'if'/'in'. Measured: 'if=[if y > 4] in=[in 2/5]', matching Stata.

primitives.name: syntax_using_element
primitives.summary: Declares a file argument; the '/' form allows the keyword using to be omitted.
primitives.openstat_note: openstat/syntax.py run() handles an element named 'using' but not the 'using/' spelling, and it requires the literal word using. Measured: 'syntax using/' + 'p foo.dta' is rc 100 'using required' here, while Stata gives rc 101 'varlist not allowed'.

primitives.name: syntax_exp_element
primitives.summary: Captures the right-hand side of a leading = as an expression, stored in the local exp.
primitives.openstat_note: openstat/syntax.py run(): the '=' element strips the = and stores 'exp'.

primitives.name: syntax_weight_element
primitives.summary: Declares that the command accepts a weight; the weight type and its expression are then available as locals.
primitives.openstat_note: openstat/syntax.py _parse_elements() has no weight branch; measured 'syntax varlist [weight]' is rc 199 'syntax descriptor not implemented: weight'. Stata 19.5 answers rc 197 for the bare [weight] spelling and leaves the aweight/wexp locals empty for [aweight].

primitives.name: syntax_option_switch
primitives.summary: Declares a yes/no option; the local named after the option is 1 when it was given and empty otherwise.
primitives.openstat_note: openstat/syntax.py _parse_option_spec() kind 'switch'; a value supplied to a switch raises 'option ... does not take a value'.

primitives.name: syntax_option_typed
primitives.summary: Declares an option that takes an argument of a stated type, with an optional default; the local holds the supplied or default value.
primitives.openstat_note: openstat/syntax.py _parse_option_spec()/_argument coercion: kinds integer, real, string, namelist, numlist, anything/passthru, with the asis flag. Measured: 'p y, level(90) verbose' sets level=90 and verbose=1.

primitives.name: program_define
primitives.summary: Defines a program from the following block, up to 'end'; the options declare what the program stores and how it may be called.
primitives.grammar: program [define] name [, rclass | eclass | sclass | sortpreserve | byable(...) | properties(...) | plugin]
primitives.openstat_note: openstat/engine.py _define_program(); PROGRAM_OPTIONS accepts rclass, eclass, sclass, sortpreserve, byable, properties and others, and _call_program() restores locals and sort order. GAP: 'nclass' is rejected (rc 198 'option nclass not allowed') although Stata accepts it.

primitives.name: program_rclass_return
primitives.summary: Stores a result in r(), or in e() when the program is declared eclass.
primitives.grammar: return scalar name = exp | return local name value
primitives.openstat_note: openstat/engine.py _return() always writes Engine.returns, so a value stored with 'return scalar' inside an eclass program is visible as r() and missing as e(). Stata routes it to e().

primitives.name: marksample
primitives.summary: Builds the 0/1 to-use marker implied by the program's last syntax command (if/in plus missing values in the varlist, and zero weights) and points a local macro at it.
primitives.grammar: marksample local [, novarlist strok zeroweight noby sysmisok]
primitives.openstat_note: openstat/program_support.py _marksample()/_syntax_marker()/_store_marker(): the marker lives in a hidden variable __NNNNNN and the named local expands to it, which is how Stata's marksample also behaves.

primitives.name: mark
primitives.summary: Creates a named marker variable: 1 where the observation is in the sample and carries no missing value, 0 elsewhere.
primitives.openstat_note: openstat/program_support.py _marksample() handles the 'mark name if ...' form but stores the result in a hidden __NNNNNN variable and only points the local at it. GAP: the variable has the requested name in Stata (byte %8.0g); here 'mark flag if g == 1' then 'describe flag' is rc 111.

primitives.name: markout
primitives.summary: Zeroes the marker for observations where any listed variable is missing, leaving the already-marked zeros alone.
primitives.openstat_note: openstat/program_support.py _markout(): reads the marker variable, ANDs in the non-missing condition (strok keeps empty strings).

primitives.name: tempvar_tempname_tempfile
primitives.summary: Allocates hidden names from one counter (__000001, ...) and, for tempfile, a path in a temporary directory.
primitives.grammar: tempvar name [name ...] | tempname name [name ...] | tempfile name [...]
primitives.openstat_note: openstat/program_support.py _temp_names()/_hidden_name(): tempvar and tempname share the counter; the values are stored as locals.

primitives.name: gettoken_args_tokenize
primitives.summary: Reads the program's positional arguments into locals, or splits a string into a first token and the rest.
primitives.grammar: args namelist | gettoken name1 name2 : string [, parse(...)] | tokenize string [, parse(...)]
primitives.openstat_note: openstat/engine.py _gettoken() (parse() supported, match() refused with rc 199) plus programming.py _tokenize().

primitives.name: missing_dot
primitives.summary: The system missing value: a numeric value that is larger than any real number and is treated as absent by every command and function.
primitives.openstat_note: openstat/expression.py _missing()/_ordered() map it to NaN and sort it last; formats.format_value() prints '.'.

primitives.name: missing_extended
primitives.summary: 26 additional numeric missing values that sort between '.' and infinity and can be stored in a dataset.
primitives.openstat_note: The expression tokenizer has no .a-.z literal, so 'display .a' is rc 198 'unsupported expression: .a' (Stata: 'a', rc 0); Engine._read() refuses any dataset containing user missing values with rc 199; metadata.py refuses them on write; mvencode is rc 199. Stata stores them and prints .a.

primitives.name: missing_function
primitives.summary: True when the argument is a missing value; both spellings are accepted.
primitives.openstat_note: openstat/expression.py Evaluator.missing() plus the 'mi' alias. Works for '.' and for empty strings; an argument written as '.a' cannot be parsed, so the extended forms are unreachable.

primitives.name: missing_ladder
primitives.summary: Stata's overflow markers come from the same ladder as .a-.z: a value that cannot be printed is shown as .<letter>_ and a genuine .<letter> as .<letter>.
primitives.openstat_note: openstat/formats.py _overflow_marker() implements the ladder L(n) = 0x7fe0010000000000 + n*2**40 (see docs/formats.md).

primitives.name: mata_st_data
primitives.summary: Reads observations of Stata variables into a Mata matrix; obs may be a range, a vector or '.' for all observations.
primitives.openstat_note: openstat/mata.py Mata.st_data(): iloc indexing over the named columns. GAP: the frame is cast to float, so reading a string variable fails with rc 199 'invalid Mata statement: could not convert string to float'.

primitives.name: mata_st_store
primitives.summary: Writes a Mata matrix back into Stata variables, checking that the shapes conform.
primitives.openstat_note: openstat/mata.py Mata.st_store(): accepts a scalar or an (len(obs) x len(varlist)) block and otherwise raises 'Mata matrices not conformable'.

primitives.name: mata_st_matrix
primitives.summary: Reads or writes a Stata matrix; Stata matrices are visible from both languages.
primitives.openstat_note: openstat/mata.py Mata.st_matrix() bridges Engine.matrices; 'matrix A = (1,2\3,4)' then 'st_matrix("A")' round-trips.

primitives.name: mata_st_numscalar
primitives.summary: Reads or writes a Stata scalar as a Mata scalar.
primitives.openstat_note: openstat/mata.py Mata.st_numscalar() bridges Engine.scalars.

primitives.name: mata_st_local
primitives.summary: Reads or writes a Stata local macro as a Mata string.
primitives.openstat_note: openstat/mata.py Mata.st_local() -> _macro(Engine.locals); measured 'st_local("back", st_local("q"))' round-trips through a local.

primitives.name: mata_st_global
primitives.summary: Reads or writes a Stata global macro as a Mata string.
primitives.openstat_note: openstat/mata.py Mata.st_global() -> _macro(Engine.globals).

primitives.name: mata_J
primitives.summary: Creates a rows x cols matrix filled with value.
primitives.openstat_note: openstat/mata.py Mata._fill() with an allocation cap (max_cells).

primitives.name: mata_I
primitives.summary: Creates the n x n identity matrix.
primitives.openstat_note: openstat/mata.py Mata._identity().

primitives.name: mata_builtins
primitives.summary: The builtin function library: matrix algebra, elementwise maths, row/column summaries, string and missing-value queries.
primitives.openstat_note: openstat/mata.py Mata._builtin() implements the matrix, maths, row/colsum, select, missing and string families; anything absent raises 'Mata function name() not implemented' (rc 199) rather than returning a guess.

primitives.name: rc_codes
primitives.summary: Every failure carries Stata's numeric return code; _rc exposes the code of the last command and capture turns a failure into a code instead of a message.
primitives.openstat_note: openstat/errors.py StataError(message, rc=198) is the single error type; Engine.rc/last_rc carry the code and 'display _rc' reports it. Codes used here include 5 (not sorted), 9 (assertion false), 100/101 (syntax), 109 (type mismatch), 110 (already defined), 111 (not found), 119, 133 (undefined c()), 197/198 (invalid syntax), 199 (not implemented), 451 (repeated time values), 459 (recast would lose information), 601 (file not found), 621/622 (preserve/restore), 693 (no graph), 2000/2001 (no observations / observation number out of range).

primitives.name: rc_fail_explicitly
primitives.summary: Anything the runtime does not implement stops with an explicit message and rc 199 instead of quietly doing something else.
primitives.openstat_note: openstat/engine.py Engine.command() ends with 'command {c} is not implemented in OpenStat' (rc 199); options are validated against an allow-list by Engine.options(), and unknown functions/descriptors raise explicitly.

primitives.name: rc_measured_divergences
primitives.summary: Where the code differs from Stata 19.5 the difference is a known, recorded gap rather than an accident.
primitives.openstat_note: Measured on this host: 'count in 0/2' rc 0 here vs 198 in Stata; 'by g: regress' 199 vs 0; 'syntax varlist [weight]' 199 vs 197; 'syntax using/' + bare file 100 vs 101; 'display .a' 198 vs 0; 'syntax varname' with a missing argument 100 (Stata: 100 too).

primitives.name: group_data
primitives.summary: Commands that read, write, reshape or describe the dataset.
primitives.openstat_note: Implemented: use save saveold import export append merge reshape collapse expand contract preserve restore keep drop rename order sort gsort duplicates generate replace egen recode encode decode destring tostring recast compress format label describe list tabulate summarize count correlate codebook inspect tabstat mean total centile. Missing (rc 199): table, collect, frame, mvencode, joinby variants beyond the implemented ones.

primitives.name: group_estimation
primitives.summary: Commands that fit a model and store the fit in e().
primitives.openstat_note: Implemented: regress, logit, logistic, probit, poisson, areg, ivregress, reghdfe, xtreg, ttest, plus the factor-variable and weight machinery in openstat/design.py. Missing: the wider estimation catalogue (glm, mixed, nbreg, tobit, ...) and every estimator that also needs postestimation support.

primitives.name: group_postestimation
primitives.summary: Commands that read the stored estimation results and produce predictions, tests or tables.
primitives.openstat_note: Implemented: predict, test, estimates store, eststo/estadd/esttab/estout (openstat/output.py). Missing (rc 199): margins with options, lincom, nlcom, estimates table, sreturn, and the [R] postestimation pages generally.

primitives.name: group_graphics
primitives.summary: Commands that draw a plot and export it.
primitives.openstat_note: Implemented: histogram/hist, kdensity, scatter, line, bar, box, dot, 'twoway scatter|line' single-plot form, and 'graph export' to PNG/SVG/PDF (openstat/graphics.py). Anything else in the graph grammar is rc 199 by design.

primitives.name: group_programming
primitives.summary: The do-file language itself: macros, control flow, programs and their support commands.
primitives.openstat_note: Implemented: local global macro foreach forvalues while if/else program syntax marksample mark markout tempvar tempname tempfile args gettoken tokenize unab levelsof numlist do run include capture quietly noisily version display return ereturn scalar matrix mata.
